summary: Rank labels by task importance, anchor them to stable scene identities, and reflow or collapse their DOM presentation without erasing access to hidden information.
objective: Labels remain legible and discoverable across viewport width, zoom, camera motion, occlusion and localization expansion while semantic reading/focus order stays intentional.
applies_when: Many objects need labels or callouts in a responsive browser view.
Some labels may be hidden visually to control crowding but must remain discoverable through selection, search, a list or details panel.
intent_signals: labels that survive narrow mobile view
hidden label remains discoverable without hover
example_prompts: Build responsive labels for a dense anatomy scene and keep every hidden structure reachable from a semantic list.
Place room labels in 3D, reflow their detail panel at narrow widths, and preserve keyboard order.
negative_signals: Treating camera distance as semantic importance.
Removing a label from both the viewport and every alternative access path.
not_for: Rasterized artistic lettering that is not interface content.
A domain-specific labeling ontology or factual naming standard.

principles: Separate anchor identity, semantic content and screen layout. World position proposes a label location; it does not determine reading order or importance.
Use a small priority ladder tied to the current task. When labels collide or leave the safe area, shorten, cluster or move lower-priority presentation while preserving an alternate discovery path.
World text may be an artistic choice. When text conveys interactive or factual meaning, keep a DOM or other semantic runtime representation with logical focus order and reflow.
implementation: In Blender, create named anchor empties or objects and optional stable custom properties. Authored in-world signs or texture text may remain meaningful; when that text conveys interactive or factual content, retain an equivalent semantic runtime representation. Export cameras/anchors and selected extras only as transport hints.

In Three.js, project anchors each frame and render semantic DOM labels with a declared collision, bounds and mesh-occlusion policy. CSS2DRenderer can host translated HTML labels but does not solve those policies.

Maintain a separate logical label list/order. On resize, language change or camera change, recompute placement without rewriting object IDs; expose selected or hidden entries through search/list/details.
observable_checks: At narrow width and enlarged text, essential controls and label details remain usable without two-dimensional page scrolling except where the spatial view itself needs two dimensions.
Tab order preserves the intended explanation rather than jumping with projected screen coordinates; selecting a hidden label reveals the same stable object.
Move an anchor behind an occluder and beyond each screen edge: the declared hide, pin, leader or list fallback occurs, and no stale label points to another object.

creative_affordances: Use typographic scale, leaders, pins or clustered badges to match the art direction.
Let artistic world lettering coexist with a plain semantic name in the runtime layer.
known_limits: CSS2DRenderer supports translation-only DOM labels and documents a 100% browser/display zoom limitation; capability and zoom behavior must be checked in the installed revision.
glTF extras carry application data but do not define DOM layout, localization, occlusion, focus order or accessibility behavior.
No viewport, assistive-technology or runtime label test was run.

claims.statement: Three.js CSS2DRenderer combines DOM elements with 3D objects using translation, ignores other renderable object types, may assign z-index by render order and camera distance, and documents support only at 100% browser/display zoom.
claims.scope: Current addon mechanism only; collision, mesh occlusion, semantic priority and responsive layout are application responsibilities.

source_refs.locator: Class description; sortObjects; 100% browser/display zoom limitation

claims.statement: WCAG 2.2 Reflow calls for vertically scrolling content without loss of information or functionality at an equivalent 320 CSS-pixel width, with exceptions where two-dimensional layout is required for meaning; Focus Order requires sequential focus to preserve meaning and operability.
claims.scope: Web interface content surrounding a spatial view; this record does not assert accessibility conformance from metadata alone.
